answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer: No, do not double your mileage. Jumping from 40 to 80 miles in one week, five weeks before a marathon, is how people pull up lame or arrive at the start line flat. Your club mate did not get to 70 in a week either; they built there over months, and their body is not your body. What wins a 3:45 marathon from where you are is not more junk miles. It is the long run creeping toward 20 to 22, one sharp marathon-pace session a week, and the easy days staying genuinely easy. That is exactly what the next few weeks do. Trust the build you are already on.

new.analysis:
## What I saw

You executed the week exactly as planned, which is the first time in this block that has happened. Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday sat at 139 bpm and 9:46/mi, Wednesday hit 8:35/mi for the marathon-pace block, and Sunday was 15 miles at 9:59 with drift of just under 6 bpm. That is a textbook build week.

## Why next week looks like this

You have four weeks of real training left before taper, so I want one more big long run and one more marathon-pace workout before we start pulling things back. The Wednesday session puts six miles at goal pace inside a ten-mile run, which is the specific stress a 3:45 finisher needs. Sunday goes to 20 miles at easy effort, matching the longest run you have done in this build, so we confirm the legs can repeat it, not just survive it once.

## About the 80-mile idea

I understand the pull of what your club mate does, but the plan that gets you under 3:45 is the one your body is actually adapted to. Doubling volume now would blow up either the Wednesday workout quality or the Sunday long run, and probably both. Both of those matter more for your race than a bigger number on the weekly total.
